Israel Election Ends in Stalemate as Netanyahu Bloc Falls Short of Majority

30 Oct 2026, 06:31 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.dw.com

3 min read

Israel's recent parliamentary elections have concluded without a clear governing majority for either major political faction, pointing toward prolonged coalition negotiations. According to figures released by the Central Election Committee (CEC) as ballots neared completion, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud-led right-wing and religious bloc secured 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

Meanwhile, the opposing centrist and liberal bloc led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot captured 48 seats. Securing a stable government requires a minimum of 61 seats, leaving both primary alliances well short of an outright majority and raising the prospect of difficult political talks.

Record Turnout and Arab Party Gains

The election saw high voter participation, with particular impact from Arab-Israeli lists. Together, Arab-Israeli parties achieved a historic milestone by winning a record 19 seats, eclipsing their previous high of 15. This strong showing could give Arab lawmakers unprecedented leverage during upcoming coalition talks, though questions remain over whether opposing factions will be willing to cooperate with them.

Following the vote, leaders of various parties have begun maneuvering. Yair Golan, chairman of the left-liberal Democrats, reported meeting with opposition figures including Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, and Ra'am party leader Mansur Abbas to discuss potential paths forward.

Fraud Claims Refuted by Authorities

In the wake of the vote, Prime Minister Netanyahu and his Likud party alleged large-scale foreign interference and voter bribery favoring Arab parties, specifically pointing toward involvement from Qatar and Turkey. Qatar's foreign ministry categorically denied the accusations, calling them a disinformation campaign.

Israeli authorities, including the Israel Police and officials from the Central Election Committee, stated there was no evidence to support the claims. Acting CEC Director General Dean Livne affirmed that the Knesset elections were conducted lawfully and that the integrity of the polling stations was rigorously safeguarded.

Next Steps and Coalition Process

President Isaac Herzog is scheduled to receive the official election results next week, after which he will consult with faction leaders before designating a lawmaker to form a government. The nominee will have 42 days to construct a working coalition. President Herzog has publicly urged all political parties to approach negotiations with an open mind to prevent another cycle of repeated elections.

Practical Implications and Verification

  • What is Confirmed: The Netanyahu-led bloc holds 53 seats and the Eisenkot-led bloc holds 48 seats, with Arab-Israeli parties taking 19 seats. Neither side has reached the 61-seat threshold required for a secure majority. The CEC confirmed that voting proceeded lawfully despite unproven fraud allegations.
  • What Remains Unknown: The exact distribution of seats could still shift slightly as the final 'double envelope' absentee ballots are processed. It remains unclear which parties will ultimately compromise to form a governing coalition or if a unity government will be pursued.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review official updates and read further reporting directly via the Deutsche Welle Live Blog.
